page: Amazon Web Services m5dn.metal is a bare-metal general-purpose server powered by dual-socket Intel Xeon Platinum 8259CL processors delivering 96 vCPUs across 48 physical cores clocked at 3.1 GHz. The architecture uses x86_64 cores with AVX-512 vector support and VNNI instructions, backed by 384 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, maintaining a balanced 4:1 memory-to-core ratio. The server includes direct hardware access via bare metal, 100 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth, and 3,600 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD instance storage. It operates without a hypervisor, exposing direct hardware virtualization and memory execution capabilities.

Benchmark outcomes show distinct throughput advantages in high-concurrency and data-intensive environments. The server demonstrates strong multi-core scalability, posting 81,985.6 on stress-ng and achieving top-tier results in PassMark multi-core, extended instruction sets, and memory benchmarks. Uncached memory read bandwidth reaches 218.93 GB/sec with 95.59 GB/sec write throughput. The platform displays high capacity in static web serving at 48.44 GB/sec and handles 77.66 million Redis SET operations per second. However, single-thread performance benchmarks such as Geekbench single-core and compression tests settle within average percentiles, reflecting its generation rather than single-core frequency focus.

The absence of dedicated GPU hardware makes this server poorly suited for transformer-based LLM token generation, where it registers in the bottom decile for generation speeds despite reasonable prompt-processing performance. Instead, its qualitative value lies in consolidating dense, I/O-intensive workloads requiring rapid local NVMe storage, broad memory bandwidth, and high network throughput on a dedicated physical host.

AWS m5dn.metal is best matched for high-throughput relational and NoSQL databases, low-latency caching tiers like Redis, static web delivery platforms, and CI/CD software compilation pipelines that fully leverage multi-threaded execution and local disk storage.
description: Amazon Web Services m5dn.metal is a bare-metal general-purpose server powered by an Intel Xeon 8259CL x86_64 processor offering 48 physical cores and 96 vCPUs at 3.1 GHz. It features 384 GB of DDR4 RAM, 3,600 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage, and a 100 Gbps baseline network interface without hypervisor overhead. In benchmarks, the server excels at multi-threaded execution, memory bandwidth, PassMark database operations, and high-frequency caching, reaching 77.66 million Redis SET operations per second and 48.44 GB/sec in static web serving. While single-thread performance remains average and text generation speeds reflect the absence of GPU acceleration, its dedicated bare-metal resources offer high efficiency for parallel tasks. The server is well positioned for enterprise database systems, high-traffic web delivery, distributed in-memory caches, and multi-core compilation tasks.
